rules_required.text: Present1sg -e and plural -að use the present stem; present2/3 require the selected mutation/consonant rules. Preterite1/3sg share the singular stem; preterite2sg uses the plural stem plus -e; all plural persons use -on. Contracted and j-present rows are explicit.
IV normally e/æ/ǣ/o. Learn niman nōm/nōmon and cuman cōm/cōmon separately; cuman present cymst/cymð.
V normally e/æ/ǣ/e. Separate palatal giefan, j-present biddan/licgan/sittan, etan longǣt, and contracted sēon/gesēon. cweðan changes ð to d in plural-based preterite and participle.

VI normally a/ō/ō/a, but j-present and palatal systems require the actual lexical rows. standan loses n in the past; slēan has short ie in present2/3 and g in past; scēop is a checked alternative to scōp.

Cook reduplicating verbs are course classVII: longēo or ē in the preterite, normally same present/participle vowel. wēpan/wōpen and fōn/fangen require explicit rows; hātan active is separate from hātte.
Preserve vowel quantity in umlaut: short ea→ie; longēa→īe; ā→ǣ;ō→ē. Dental combinations and geminate reduction are inherited rules. x plus either -st or -ð gives -xt: weaxan2/3sg both wiext.
biddan/licgan/sittan/hębban/scieppan have explicit consonant patterns; swęrian uses -ie/-est/-eð/-iað present endings like nęrian, but a strong swōr/swōron preterite.
geswīcan/scīnan/flēogan/swimman are new productive lexical systems applying already taught classesI–III. Prior supplied tokens are not prior mastery.
Four principal parts identify stems. Infinitives and participles remain supplied citations with no independent nonfinite recall or syntax; neither passive nor perfect follows from a table.
gesēon and gescieppan are independently evidenced lexemes. Prefix-preserving finite expansion is declared; arbitrary prefix attachment or semantic inference is not taught.

Finite morphology does not determine government. New composed clauses use only the bounded frames in lexical-frames.json and prior taught adjuncts; other selected verbs may be assessed by labelled morphology.

Exceptional contracted rejoice system and consonant/vowel alternatives, with no participle printed in the Cook row. Unassigned rather than inventing a fourth part.
Additional regular and dental examples; etan and cweðan cover selected dental behavior. Long mǣt noted by Cook belongs to unassigned metan.
Exceptional laugh past hlōh/hlōgon, no participle printed in the source row. Unassigned rather than incomplete productive or recognition paradigm.

Additional classVI lexical systems actually named by Cook: the first three follow faran, lēan/ðwēan follow slēan, and stæppan belongs to the j-subclass. Their senses, complements and all twelve cells have not been assigned.
bannan preterite is described as very rare; gangan has the additional gān substitution. Keep explicit unassigned catalogue rather than pretending these are regular productive targets.
Additional VII examples. weaxan chosen for exercise grow; grōwan remains documented valid lexical alternative needing scaffold/full audit before recall. Distinguish blāwan blow from blōwan bloom.
Additional ē-past and contracted examples. Cook rǣdan usually weak; these lexical exceptions are not hidden under a predictive class formula.
